reason: Rectilinear (rectiligne) calyx tubes, sutures and nerves are free of curves; PATO:0002180 straight. The examples contrast it with 'slightly curved'.

This states that a part (lamella of the orchid lip disc) is absent, but neither PO nor FLOPO has a lamella class, so no absence rule can be written. Add the bearer first, then this becomes an entity_absence rule.
Dicoccous means splitting into two cocci, which is a count of 2 mericarps (PO_0020075) in the fruit. That is the count pattern, not a quality term.
French anastomosées veins rejoin one another to form a network; FLOPO:0991128 anastomosing inheres in the veins.

label: catenate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting of, or being borne as, units joined end to end in a chain.
reason: Used for chains of tubers, chains of hair cells and rachis/costa segments. FLOPO:0991168 moniliform is the bead-like shape of one structure with constrictions, not units linked end to end.

label: triplicate
definition: A folded quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being folded back on itself twice, so that it runs in three parallel limbs in an S-shaped course. NOTE: Used for anther thecae (e.g. Cucurbitaceae); sibling of FLOPO:0991123 conduplicate.
reason: Thecae triplicate are folded twice into three parallel parts. PATO:0001989 sinuous does not express the folding.
French oppositifolié is a mistranslation of 'leaf-opposed': inflorescences that arise opposite a leaf; FLOPO:0991001.
Pulpeux fruits and mesocarps are soft and fleshy; PATO:0002351 fleshy is the nearest existing term. 'pulpeux-fibreux' is a compound of two values and goes through the continuum pattern.
French plan-convexe is plano-convex: flat on one side and convex on the other; FLOPO:0991184.

Radicant stems root at the nodes or at the base, which means adventitious (shoot-borne) roots are present. This matches the note on 'rooting at the nodes' in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md. The position 'at the nodes' goes in slot 1.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum/compound of two values: sericeous PATO_0104358 + tomentose PATO_0002341)
reason: This joins two existing values (sericeous, tomentose) on one bearer, a hyphenated compound like 'oblong-ovate'. Treat it as the compound of the two values, not as a new term.
Pit-like glands and domatia are small hollows set below the surrounding surface; PATO:0002416 sunken. PATO:0002296 foveate is a surface marked with many pits and does not fit a single gland.
'With aerenchyma' or 'à aérenchyme' states that the part is present: PO:0005702 aerenchyma (with root, stem and leaf aerenchyma PO_0006213/4/5 as the more specific classes).
Moundlike plants and stigmas are rounded and dome-like; PATO:0001789 domed.

A falsely petiolate leaf has its blade narrowed at the base into a stalk-like part that is not a true petiole ('narrowed to falsely petiolate'). PATO:0001500 tapered, as for 'narrowed'. It must not map to FLOPO:0991023 petiolate.
A plain negation of PATO:0104353 reflexed (French non réfléchi).
An adverb that only qualifies the division word it stands with ('ternately compound', 'ternately cut'). On its own it is a fragment.
Semispherical means half a sphere; PATO:0005000 hemispheroid.
Glands are absent. Gland maps to PO:0005656 by the bearer rule of the previous review (C265).

Basiscopic pinnules or lobes are the ones on the side facing the base of the frond. That picks out which part is meant (a position of the bearer), like 'basal leaves'; it is not a quality of that part.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (two values on one bearer: acute (sensu botany) FLOPO:0991095 + asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: An obliquely acute base is both acute and unequal-sided. Both values exist, so this is a compound of two values and needs no new term.

Recumbent shrubs, branches and pitchers lie on the ground; PATO:0000631 prostrate. Limit the rule to these bearers: 'accombant' embryos and seeds (accumbent cotyledons in Brassicaceae) are a different term and must not take this rule.
'Densely set (with hairs or scales)' needs what the part is set with; the covering and its density are the quality, as for 'covered'.
Vague: it does not say in what way the exostome, endostome or marginal cells differ.

target: new: presence with frequency (part present, frequency_qualifier rarely)
reason: 'Turions uncommon', 'tendrils uncommon' say how often a part is present across plants, not a quality of the part. It is a presence with a frequency qualifier, as in docs/odp/08-alternative-with-frequency.md.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: hexagonal PATO_0002509 + elongated PATO_0001154)
reason: Long-hexagonal moss leaf cells are hexagonal and longer than wide. Both values exist, so this is a compound and needs no new term.
French uniséminé means 1-seeded: a count of 1 seed (PO_0009010). 'seeded' is already in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.

French soudés (entre eux) is like parts fused together (sepals, petals, filaments, styles); FLOPO:0991067 connate, as for 'united'. Where a second, different part is named ('soudés à la corolle'), FLOPO:0991129 adnate applies.

It would negate 'marginate' (having a distinct border), which has no PATO or FLOPO term (PATO:0002234 emarginate means notched and is different). Raise 'marginate' first, then this becomes a negated value.
A mistranslation of French paniculé(e) (racemes or cymes arranged in a panicle). The architecture is FLOPO:0991198 panicle-like.
